items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: The interviewee discusses Jack Lane's band and its reputation ('If you didn't have any good air with Jack Lane, you wouldn't know a musician') but does not state that he personally played in, toured with, or collaborated directly with Jack Lane. He mentions playing with 'Christian' and his father, b

ctx.x: Well, I was going to ask you a little bit more about Papa Jack Lane's band, his dance band. They weren't legitimate sounding. How did they sound? How were they? Very good. Very good.

One man, the Pembert of Born here, to hear what he was going to do, to catch it. If you didn't have any good air with Jack Lane, you wouldn't know a musician. Air comes with him and everything. You had to be what they call fake musician. And it was strictly jazz, wasn't it? Strictly.
Fake musician. No, there wasn't any legitimate sound like the Robichoke band. No, no, no. Nothing like that.
